questions.question_text: In Systems Theory, which of the following best describes a family business?

options.A: A completely closed system with no interaction with the external environment
options.B: A system driven only by customer feedback
options.C: A system in which family, ownership, and management are interconnected
options.D: A system where ownership and management always remain separate

questions.explanation: Correct answer: A system in which family, ownership, and management are interconnected.

questions.question_text: In the framework discussed, which of the following comes immediately after family involvement?

options.D: Economic performance

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Family behavioural disposition.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the three core dimensions of ownership competence?

options.D: Marketing competence

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Marketing competence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the role of governance in this framework?

options.A: It helps align family goals with business goals
options.B: It focuses only on increasing financial returns
options.C: It refers only to family ownership of the firm
options.D: It represents the firm’s physical and financial assets

questions.explanation: Correct answer: It helps align family goals with business goals.

questions.question_text: Which type of capital refers to the relationships and connections a family builds with employees, suppliers, customers, and the wider community?

options.D: Social capital

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Social capital.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a family-oriented non-economic goal?

options.D: Expanding into a new geographic market

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Maintaining family harmony and reputation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best explains the longevity of many family firms discussed in this session?

options.A: A strong focus on short-term quarterly returns
options.D: A combination of intergenerational continuity, adaptability, and long-term investment

questions.explanation: Correct answer: A combination of intergenerational continuity, adaptability, and long-term investment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best reflects a key theme from the session?

options.A: Industrialisation replaced family businesses with professionally managed firms
options.B: Family firms during the industrial era operated only within local markets
options.C: Industrial family firms avoided involvement in infrastructure and finance
options.D: Family firms played a major role in industrial capitalism and were often closely connected with national political developments

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Family firms played a major role in industrial capitalism and were often closely connected with national political developments.

questions.question_text: What role did the hundi play in pre-colonial and early colonial India?

options.A: It functioned as an early transferable bill of exchange
options.B: It was used only for local cash payments
options.C: It was a government-issued tax document
options.D: It was a form of family inheritance

questions.explanation: Correct answer: It functioned as an early transferable bill of exchange.

questions.question_text: According to the session, what does “saakh” primarily refer to?

options.D: Political influence

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Reputational trust.

questions.question_text: What was a key feature of the Managing Agency System?

options.A: Managing agents controlled several companies while contributing only a small share of the risk capital
options.B: Managing agents owned all the capital of the companies they controlled
options.C: Managing agents were appointed only by the government
options.D: Managing agents were prohibited from handling day-to-day operations

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Managing agents controlled several companies while contributing only a small share of the risk capital.

questions.question_text: Which of the following was a common response of Indian family businesses to liberalisation after 1991?

options.D: Returning to closely held family-only operations

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Restructuring businesses and professionalising management.

questions.question_text: How did many Indian family business groups respond to the regulatory constraints of the License Raj?

options.A: They completely withdrew from regulated industries
options.B: They avoided diversification and remained in a single sector
options.C: They relied only on foreign capital for expansion
options.D: They navigated licensing rules, diversified into accessible sectors, and restructured ownership

questions.explanation: Correct answer: They navigated licensing rules, diversified into accessible sectors, and restructured ownership.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is highlighted as a major social contribution of family firms?

options.C: Supporting employment, philanthropy, and community development
options.D: Focusing only on shareholder returns

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Supporting employment, philanthropy, and community development.

questions.question_text: What was one of the key findings of the Anderson and Reeb 2003 study?

options.A: Family firms consistently underperformed non-family firms
options.B: Family ownership had no relationship with firm performance
options.C: Family firms performed better only when managed by outside professionals
options.D: Family firms performed better on average than non-family firms

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Family firms performed better on average than non-family firms.

questions.question_text: According to the alignment–entrenchment trade-off, when is family firm performance likely to be strongest?

options.B: When family ownership is extremely low
options.C: When family ownership is completely absent
options.D: When family control is maximised at all costs

questions.explanation: Correct answer: When family ownership is moderate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is identified as an important firm-level driver of longevity in family businesses?

options.D: Relying only on family members for management

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Strong governance and well-planned succession.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best represents strategic control in a family business?

options.A: Deciding which suppliers to work with on a daily basis
options.B: Determining the long-term direction and future scope of the business
options.C: Managing employee attendance and daily tasks
options.D: Monitoring routine operational processes

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Determining the long-term direction and future scope of the business.

questions.question_text:
Match the following factors to their descriptions:

Options:
- Political stability
- Consolidated ownership
- Professionalisation
- Flexible successor selection
- Craft and heritage sectors
- Predictable inheritance laws
- Succession planning
- Family governance

Matches:
- Supports smoother transfer of ownership
- Creates structures such as family councils and constitutions
- Helps ensure leadership continuity across generations
- Reduces sudden disruptions to the business environment
- Helps preserve family control and capital
- Brings non-family expertise into management
- Expands the pool of capable future leaders
- Benefit from slowly changing skills and production methods
questions.explanation:
Answer:
Supports smoother transfer of ownership → Predictable inheritance laws
Creates structures such as family councils and constitutions → Family governance
Helps ensure leadership continuity across generations → Succession planning
Reduces sudden disruptions to the business environment → Political stability
Helps preserve family control and capital → Consolidated ownership
Brings non-family expertise into management → Professionalisation
Expands the pool of capable future leaders → Flexible successor selection
Benefit from slowly changing skills and production methods → Craft and heritage sectors

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors is highlighted as contributing to the resilience of family firms during crises?

options.A: Higher dependence on short-term market sentiment
options.B: Greater emphasis on rapid expansion during downturns
options.C: Stronger relationships, disciplined capital allocation, and better access to credit
options.D: Avoidance of all restructuring decisions

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Stronger relationships, disciplined capital allocation, and better access to credit.

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the Entrepreneurial Family Galaxy?

options.A: It places the family at the centre and views different entities as vehicles serving different family objectives
options.B: It focuses only on the family’s main operating company
options.C: It refers only to the financial investments made by a family
options.D: It explains how family members compete for ownership

questions.explanation: Correct answer: It places the family at the centre and views different entities as vehicles serving different family objectives.

questions.question_text:
Categorize the following companies into the four ownership and management quadrants:

Options:
- Mahindra
- Reliance
- Apollo Hospitals
- Marico
- Wipro
- TCS
- Suzlon
- Max Financial

Categories:
- High family ownership + family managed
- High family ownership + professionally managed
- Low family ownership + family managed
- Low family ownership + professionally managed
questions.explanation:
Answer:
High family ownership + family managed → Reliance, Apollo Hospitals, Suzlon
High family ownership + professionally managed → Marico, Wipro, TCS
Low family ownership + family managed → Mahindra
Low family ownership + professionally managed → Max Financial

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a key strength of family businesses discussed in this session?

options.A: A strong focus on short-term quarterly performance
options.C: A long-term perspective supported by patient capital
options.D: Frequent changes in ownership and leadership

questions.explanation: Correct answer: A long-term perspective supported by patient capital.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most likely to become a weakness in a family business?

options.B: Deep relationships with employees and customers
options.D: Excessive dependence on the founder for key decisions

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Excessive dependence on the founder for key decisions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best distinguishes a family business from a non-family business?

options.A: Family businesses always avoid external professionals
options.B: Family businesses are typically guided by long-term family values and succession considerations
options.C: Non-family businesses do not focus on shareholder value
options.D: Family businesses cannot raise debt

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Family businesses are typically guided by long-term family values and succession considerations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best reflects Stewardship Theory in a family business?

options.A: A manager focuses mainly on maximising personal rewards
options.B: An owner and manager always have conflicting goals
options.C: A manager acts in the long-term interests of the business and aligns with the family’s goals
options.D: A family member automatically eliminates all agency costs

questions.explanation: Correct answer: A manager acts in the long-term interests of the business and aligns with the family’s goals.

questions.question_text: According to Stakeholder Theory, which of the following should a firm consider when making decisions?

options.A: Only the interests of shareholders, suppliers, and employees
options.B: Only the interests of family members and customers
options.D: The interests of employees, customers, suppliers, owners, and other stakeholders

questions.explanation: Correct answer: The interests of employees, customers, suppliers, owners, and other stakeholders.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT part of the FIBER framework?

options.D: Identification with the family business

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Financial profitability.

questions.question_text: According to Transaction Cost Economics, when is a firm more likely to perform an activity internally rather than outsource it?

options.B: When performing the activity internally is less costly than using the external market
options.C: When the firm wants to avoid all external relationships
options.D: When the activity involves only financial assets

questions.explanation: Correct answer: When performing the activity internally is less costly than using the external market.

questions.question_text: In the Resource-Based View of family business, what does “familiness” refer to?

options.A: A unique bundle of resources created through the interaction of the family and the business
options.B: The number of family members working in the firm
options.C: The financial wealth owned by the family
options.D: The legal ownership structure of the firm

questions.explanation: Correct answer: A unique bundle of resources created through the interaction of the family and the business.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best explains why the three-generation rule should be interpreted with caution?

options.A: All family businesses survive beyond the third generation
options.B: Definitions of survival may ignore changes in ownership, management, or business structure
options.C: Family ownership always remains concentrated across generations
options.D: Third-generation family members always prefer to leave the business

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Definitions of survival may ignore changes in ownership, management, or business structure.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is one possible pathway for transferring a family business to the next generation?

options.B: Dividing the business among family members
options.D: Retaining all decision-making with the incumbent

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Dividing the business among family members.

questions.question_text: How does the role of the successor typically change during the succession process?

options.A: It remains unchanged until the final handover
options.B: It immediately replaces the incumbent's role
options.C: It is limited only to ownership decisions
options.D: It gradually increases as the incumbent’s role decreases

questions.explanation: Correct answer: It gradually increases as the incumbent’s role decreases.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes a complete succession in a family business?

options.C: Transfer of both ownership control and management control
options.D: Appointment of a professional manager without any change in control

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Transfer of both ownership control and management control.

questions.question_text: Which type of incumbent is most likely to support a smooth succession by stepping back while continuing to mentor the successor?

options.D: Controller

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Ambassador.

questions.question_text: Which succession path is most likely to help a successor build credibility through independent professional experience before joining the family business?

options.D: Remaining only a passive owner

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Working outside and then returning.

questions.question_text: What type of commitment arises when a successor joins because of family expectations or a sense of obligation?
questions.explanation: Answer: Normative commitment

questions.question_text: What term describes the continued influence of the founder even after leadership has been transferred?
questions.explanation: Answer: Founder's shadow

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most important for a successor to earn credibility in the family business?

options.D: Immediate authority over all employees

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Competence, commitment, and earned respect.

questions.question_text: What type of incumbent plans the exit and continues as a mentor or advisor without trying to regain control?
questions.explanation: Answer: Ambassador

questions.question_text: What type of succession passes the business to the eldest child?
questions.explanation: Answer: Primogeniture

questions.question_text: What type of succession involves ownership being shared among multiple family members?
questions.explanation: Answer: Coparcenary

questions.question_text: What is the term for transferring the business to the next generation without dividing it?
questions.explanation: Answer: Undivided transfer

questions.question_text: What do we call the person who currently leads the family business and is expected to transfer control?
questions.explanation: Answer: Incumbent

questions.question_text: A successor is highly willing to join the family business but currently lacks the required competence and experience. How would this person be classified?

options.D: Reluctant talent

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Eager apprentice.

questions.question_text: What term describes an incumbent expecting the successor to behave and lead exactly like them?
questions.explanation: Answer: Clone syndrome

questions.question_text: What does professionalisation primarily change in a family business?

options.D: The industry in which the firm operates

questions.explanation: Correct answer: How decisions are made.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a key benefit of professionalisation?

options.D: Merit-based talent management

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Merit-based talent management.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best defines a professional manager?

options.A: A manager who uses expertise, objective criteria, and professional standards
options.B: A manager who is not a family member
options.C: A manager who relies mainly on personal relationships
options.D: A manager who holds ownership shares

questions.explanation: Correct answer: A manager who uses expertise, objective criteria, and professional standards.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is one of the variables that shapes the professionalisation process?

options.D: Office location alone

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Family characteristics.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the three paths to professionalisation?

options.D: Hiring external professionals

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Avoiding all formal management roles.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is one of the types of professionalised family firms discussed in the module?

options.D: Hybrid professional firm

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Hybrid professional firm.

questions.question_text: Why is innovation described as a paradox in family businesses?

options.A: Family firms never invest in innovation
options.B: Family control can both support and restrict innovation
options.C: Innovation is only relevant to non-family firms
options.D: Family firms always prefer radical innovation

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Family control can both support and restrict innovation.

questions.question_text: Which theory views internationalisation as a gradual process of learning and increasing commitment?

options.D: Institutional View

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Uppsala Model.

questions.question_text: Which entry mode generally involves the highest level of control and resource commitment?

options.D: Wholly owned subsidiary

questions.explanation: Correct answer: Wholly owned subsidiary.
